claims.text: A DFT-level two-phase coexistence simulation can predict the melting temperature of refractory materials.
A DFT-level two-phase coexistence simulation can predict the entropy and enthalpy of fusion of refractory materials.
A DFT-level two-phase coexistence simulation can predict the volume change at the melting point of refractory materials.
The proposed enhanced sampling method is more computationally efficient than traditional ab initio thermodynamic integration.
The proposed method retains accuracy comparable to traditional ab initio thermodynamic integration.
The method can efficiently sample a free-energy landscape at a solid-liquid interface while capturing phase coexistence.
Direct simulation of coexisting solid and liquid phases bypasses costly thermodynamic-integration paths.
Bypassing thermodynamic-integration paths reduces computational expense.
The reduction in computational cost is sufficient to make high-throughput screening feasible.
Systems with extremely complex phase behavior may reduce the accuracy of the proposed method.
Near critical points, significant dynamical effects may challenge the accuracy of the proposed method.
Some refractory systems with subtle phase transitions may require further calibration.
